name: Essential Pentosuria

criteria.description: Presence of L-xylulose in urine detected by specific biochemical assays
Demonstration of deficient L-xylulose reductase activity in erythrocytes or liver tissue
Normal blood glucose levels to exclude diabetes mellitus
Lack of clinical symptoms or metabolic derangements despite pentosuria

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of urinary L-xylulose with confirmed L-xylulose reductase deficiency and exclusion of diabetes mellitus
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies on biochemical testing and exclusion of other causes of reducing substances in urine

laboratory: Positive Benedict’s test for reducing substances in urine
Normal blood glucose and HbA1c levels
Deficient erythrocyte L-xylulose reductase enzyme activity
other: No significant clinical abnormalities despite biochemical findings

distinguishingFeatures: Hyperglycemia with elevated blood glucose and HbA1c
Positive glucose oxidase test in urine
Presence of clinical symptoms such as polyuria, polydipsia, and weight loss
Presence of fructose in urine instead of L-xylulose

redFlags: Persistent hyperglycemia indicating possible misdiagnosis of diabetes
Presence of clinical symptoms such as weight loss or ketoacidosis
Positive glucose oxidase urine test inconsistent with pentosuria
references: Scriver CR, Beaudet AL, Sly WS, Valle D. The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. McGraw-Hill; 2001.
